title: Watercooler Entry Node
description: Schema for a single entry node on the baseline graph (orphan branch). Authority-ladder provenance fields (Phase 1a, v0.10 §5.4.1 / §10.2.1 / §10.5 / §10.6) are optional, unenforced descriptive metadata — the server-side write check that formerly consumed them was removed. Parity-bound with src/watercooler/baseline_graph/writer.py:EntryData and (cross-repo) watercooler-site TypeScript bindings.

body.description: Markdown body. First line should be Spec: <spec>.

code_branch.description: Optional. Branch tag on the entry; not a storage dimension.

decision_origin.description: Phase 1a (v0.10 §10.6). How the entry came to exist.

authority_source.description: Phase 1a (v0.10 §10.2.1). Optional, unenforced provenance metadata identifying the authorizing source for a Decision/Closure. The server-side write check that formerly required it was removed; the daemon no longer stamps it.

authority_basis.description: Phase 1a (v0.10 §5.4.1). Evidence-light Decision lint requires this on Decision entries.

source_entry_id.description: Phase 1a. ULID of the source entry for promotions (the candidate Note) or daemon extractions (the entry the LLM extracted from).

human_authorized_by.description: Phase 1b (#879). Optional, unenforced. The accountable human or institution for a human-authorized or human-promoted Decision/Closure, as a namespace-qualified identifier (e.g. 'github:<login>' or 'wc:user:<handle>'); never a bare email. PRIVACY: this value is append-only, git-committed, and federation-visible — it cannot be redacted later, so prefer a stable handle or opaque account id over raw PII. Distinct from actor_class (which records the writer): an agent-executed write performed under human authorization records actor_class='agent' with the accountable human here. A single principal for now; multi-principal co-authorization is a future extension.

confidence.description: Phase 1a. LLM extraction confidence. 1-5 is the rubric used by the extractor's gates and persisted Decision entries with a meaningful score; 0 is a sentinel emitted on rejection shapes (llm_unavailable, llm_parse_failure) where no usable confidence was produced. Schema floor is 0 to round-trip both shapes; consumers that need a usable score should treat 0 as 'no signal' rather than as a valid rating.

gate_results.description: Phase 1a. 8-gate validation outcomes from LLM extraction.

support_counts.description: #896 Leg 2 (§6 tether read-model, #881). Per-tether support counts (source/record_state/test/contract/user/interpretive/unknown), strongest-first, non-zero entries only. The primary support surface — never collapsed into a single confidence number or badge.

dominant_tether.description: #896 Leg 2. The strongest *present* tether — a salience hint for rendering order, NOT an authority badge. 'unknown' when there is no support.

thin_support.description: #896 Leg 2. True when no substantive (source/record_state/test/contract/user) support backs the surface.

thin_support_reason.description: #896 Leg 2. Deterministic one-line explanation when thin_support is true; absent otherwise.

support_evidence.description: #896 Leg 2. Per-support inspection pointers so a consumer can drill to the actual quote/record rather than trust a bare count (the §6 inspect-don't-trust substrate).

legacy_extraction_policy_status.description: Historical metadata only. A one-time Phase 4h migration (#868) stamped the value `pre_policy` on a fixed set of legacy daemon-extracted Decision nodes that predate the Phase 1a provenance work. Not part of EntryData and not written by any current code — the backfill script and the server-side enforcement engine were removed in #872. Present on those pre-existing nodes by design (threads are append-only); optional, never required.
